description: Viewer lane labels for one ledger row and its receipt file (FIXER rules V-PRECEDENCE, V-FAILED-READ, V-UNKNOWN-SETTLED, V-LINK-GREY, plus known defects KD-1/KD-2). receipt: an object, a raw string (written as is) or null (no file). Chip text "DISAGREE" stands for rules.constants.DISAGREE. reservation: the value on the row's 'reservation' line, or "absent". greens: every c-green chip in the row. label_rules names the FIXER rules (rules.json viewer_label_rules) a vector pins; on a known_defect vector they are the rules its target follows and today's output breaks. The label-requester vectors pin the limits of a requester paid row. Swarm audit of 8ddc5d2, finding 5: the row has a job budget, worked out from the job's own running total. Finding 13: the daily cap bounds every call the seat's key pays for, so the row is checked against the seat's daily cap (spent_before, the seat's spend today), then its job budget (job_spent_before, the job's requester spend). A requester row with no job_spent_before was written before finding 13: its spent_before is the job's spend. Review of the audit 8ddc5d2 fixes: the daily cap applies to every row, whatever its payer. A payer that is neither holder nor requester is checked against the daily cap. A limit that applies and cannot be worked out bars the green chain final chip: one amber '<limit> not checked' chip stands in its place and the row keeps 'matches'. On the row with no job_spent_before the job budget is worked out from spent_before and the daily cap is not checked. The label-settled-amount-unknown vectors and the two label-disagree controls after them pin finding 6: settled on both sides with both amounts unknown is agreement, with its own amber label. The label-negative vectors pin finding 7: a negative amount is unknown. The cap-charge vectors pin item 2 of the review of the audit 8ddc5d2 fixes: a settled row whose cap charge is a known amount that is not its settled spend shows a 'cap charge' line, with the ledger reason beside it when there is one, and nothing else on the row changes. Their rule viewer.cap_charge_line gives line: the visible text of the row's 'cap charge' line, or "absent". Vectors with status known_defect assert today's output in expect; target is not asserted. The exact-spend vectors (money stage 1) use rule viewer.exact_spend: line is the visible text of the row's 'exact spend' line, or "absent"; spend_raw is the base unit digits in the row data, or null; differs says whether the row carries the flag that the exact amount differs from the receipt. The below-hold vectors (hold floor, rules.json KD-12) use rule viewer.below_hold: below_hold says whether the row carries the spend flag 'charged below its hold', bad whether the row is marked bad, and greens every c-green chip in it.
